text: Hoping to get the treasure for himself at last, Tom went back to the swamp and found the dark woodsman strolling along with his axe on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> This time Tom agreed to the bargain, but there was one condition, that the treasure must be used in the devils service. <break time="0.8s" /> The devil first suggested a slave ship, but Tom refused, for wicked as he was, even the devil could not tempt him to become a slave trader. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the devil proposed that Tom become a usurer, a moneylender who charges very high interest, and this was exactly to Toms taste. <break time="0.8s" /> You shall lend money at two percent a month, said the devil, and Tom eagerly replied that he would charge four. <break time="0.8s" /> Within a few days, Tom was seated behind a desk in Boston at a time when money was scarce and many people badly needed loans. <break time="0.8s" /> He grew rich quickly, and in proportion to the distress of each borrower was the hardness of his terms. <break time="0.8s" /> As Tom grew old, however, he began to worry about his bargain, and he suddenly became a loud and eager churchgoer. <break time="0.8s" /> He always carried a small Bible in his coat pocket, hoping that it would protect him if the devil ever came to collect.
